lines.text: There's an easy-looking fix. Every drive motor has a current limit. Less current, less push. So why not set it low and never slip?
Current, written I, is measured in amps, and drawn teal.
Our limit is k slip current, in Tuner Constants: three hundred sixty amps. That's far more than a wheel needs to break loose.
In twenty twenty-six, our team learned why it stays high. When the robot speeds up, its weight shifts onto the back wheels.
Heavier wheels could push harder. But a low current limit chops every wheel down to the same small push.
Our simulator agrees. With the center of mass twenty centimeters up, sixty amps was zero point four four seconds slower, with one point seven times the odometry error.
So the current limit is only a ceiling, a safety net. It is not the plan.
The plan lives in a class called Acceleration Limiter. To build it, we need four ideas: grip, weight, turning, and motors.
